The fog hangs over the turbulent sea like liquid lead, spreading into a dense, treacherous net that swallows everything beneath it.
Fog and storm clouds merge until sea and sky seem pressed together. The lookout's latest report is unchanged: Visibility still shows no sign of improving.

Red First Officer
Ma'am, the Gray fleet still hasn't made any visible move. Signal detection confirms that their flagship remains silent.
Adelyde
No signal from the flagship doesn't mean they're doing nothing.

The flagship's silence doesn't match the engine noise reported earlier. The most likely explanation is that Gray's destroyers have slipped into the reef belt under cover of the fog, with every signal light shut off. They're moving through the channels like ghosts.
Adelyde
Lights out, radio silence, destroyers inside the reef belt...
Adelyde
They're hiding.
Assets/Product/Texture/Image/IconMovie/V480haituNormal01.png
She returns to the chart table, enlarges the reef map, and taps several key positions in turn.
Her opponent has reached the same conclusion she would have. Gray is already concealed inside the reefs.
She can't stop a concealed maneuver she can't see, but the geography can still tell her where they're most likely to emerge.
Adelyde
Flank patrols, widen your search radius. Station one destroyer at every major exit along the outer reef belt, and maintain visual contact.
Adelyde
Pay particular attention to these three exits.
Red First Officer
These three? But the eastern exit has a wider natural channel. Wouldn't that let them deploy more destroyers?
Adelyde
These three chokepoints offer the best positions for turning a retreat into an attack. They're more valuable than the wider eastern passage.
Red First Officer
Understood!
She reviews the positions around the main channel exit once more. She deliberately leaves the forces there unchanged, partly because she wants to see what this student does next.
After all, anyone who can quickly turn the fog and terrain into an opportunity for a stealth operation is worth watching.
In their place, she'd use one of those chokepoints to stage a feint. The question is whether her opponent will do the same.
For now, the safest choice is to watch and wait.
Assets/Product/Effect/Prefab/FxUi/FxUiStory/FxUiStoryBlackPassScene.prefab
The first change comes a few minutes later.
Red First Officer
Multiple vessel signals detected near the western reef exit! Possible Gray destroyer formations moving toward our flank!
Red First Officer
Ma'am, should we split our forces and reinforce the western flank?
Adelyde
Show me the readings.
Adelyde moves to the detection console. The scenario comes from an era when radar was still primitive, so the readings are far from precise.
Even so, the crude display tells her enough.
Movement patterns, signal strength, timing between echoes—the radar can't provide an exact position, but coordinates aren't the only useful information.
It's too uniform.

Destroyers moving through the reef belt should produce broken, uneven signals as the rocks block and reveal them. These echoes are too steady, spaced almost perfectly apart, as though the sources were moving in straight lines across open water.
Adelyde
It's a decoy.
Red First Officer
You mean... the signals aren't coming from actual ships?
Adelyde
Exactly. The readings are too clean.
Adelyde
It's a feint. These are false signals. The destroyers are somewhere else.
Adelyde
The idea is sound, but the bait is too obvious.
She places one finger on the western exit, then traces it across the chart toward the main channel.
Adelyde
Flank patrols, hold your positions. No reinforcements. Main fleet, full speed toward the main channel exit. Secure a blockade before they can reach it.
Red First Officer
Yes!
As the first officer opens the hatch to carry out the order, a soldier outside is about to enter with a report.
After hearing the soldier's report, the first officer turns back.
Red First Officer
Acoustic signatures detected at the northern reef exit! Gray destroyers appear to be attempting a breakout!
The northern exit.
Not west. North.

If the western signals are the feint and the real attack is coming from the north, what do they hope to gain? Even if they destroy the patrol ships there, the dense reefs will only allow shallow-draft vessels through. That alone isn't worth the effort.
Adelyde
Is this a second move meant to split my forces, or did they simply stumble into it?
Adelyde

All units, adjust formation. Main fleet, slow down. Do not push forward. Port-side destroyers, intercept the northern formation. Starboard destroyers, move around the main channel exit and cut off the enemy flagship's route.
Assets/Product/Texture/Image/BgStory/BgStory1595.jpg
Inside Gray's operations room...
The first formation's buoy signals have held for twelve minutes. The latest readings confirm that Red hasn't committed any major forces to the western flank.
They didn't take the bait...
You had a backup plan, but having your opening move seen through is still frustrating.
Red's response has been almost effortless, as though the entire battle is already under their control.
Yet that very confidence raises another question.
The tactical simulation system is certainly capable of recognizing a feint. On higher difficulties, its tactical database can issue responses almost instantly.
But their response doesn't feel reactive. It feels deliberate, as if they had planned for this all along.

You deliberately made the false signals uniform enough to be discovered. It was a standard misdirection tactic. Once the system saw through it, the optimal response should've been to ignore the decoy and push directly toward the main channel exit.
But they didn't.

They saw through the feint and identified the real attack, yet they never rushed. Instead, they calmly accounted for every possibility—the port destroyers moved to intercept the northern group, the starboard destroyers circled toward the exit, and the main fleet slowed down to observe.
Three separate movements, all unfolding at once, each with a different purpose.
They're preparing for every possible outcome, weaving a larger net around an opponent who thought they were the hunter.
A system chooses the mathematically optimal answer because it can calculate every branch to its conclusion. A person facing incomplete information is more likely to choose the safest answer instead.
If the opponent is a real person...
You shake off the thought. This isn't the time to dwell on it.
The window is closing.
The second formation is already waiting at the northern exit, while the flagship's engines idle at low power, ready to accelerate the moment the order comes.
Gray First Officer
Commandant, judging by the sea, the wind's about to pick up.
Gray First Officer
The fog may clear sooner than I expected.
How much time do you think we have?
Gray First Officer
Sorry, Commandant, but I can't say for sure. The weather here changes too quickly.
Gray First Officer
I can tell you this, though—rain is coming. The air always smells different before a heavy storm.
Understood.
The report makes the decision even more urgent.
There are two options.
The first is to keep waiting, extend the feint, and force Red to keep questioning every movement until a genuine opening appears.
The second is to launch the northern attack now, strike and withdraw, then drive the flagship toward the main channel exit while Red is dealing with the damage.
You run both possibilities through your mind and make your decision.
Choose Option One
Choose Option Two
Waiting is no longer an option. Once the fog clears, one of your few remaining advantages will disappear with it.
This is the only path left. It will cost you, but every gamble comes with a price.
Second formation, attack through the northern exit. Target the port side of their battleship.
Fire three rapid volleys, then withdraw into the reef belt immediately. Don't stay and fight.
The moment the northern guns open fire, the flagship will move at full speed through the central deep-water channel.
Our objective is the anchorage at the main channel exit.
Gray First Officer
Commandant, the window is too narrow! Our flagship's starboard side will be exposed to the enemy's forward destroyers!
We can take the hit.
They haven't moved close enough. At this range, we can take one volley and still reach the anchorage.
We have to control the main channel.
The first officer pauses, then understands what's at stake.
Gray First Officer
Understood. We'll execute the plan!
The thought that Red may be controlled by a real person still lingers. If that's true, their forward interceptors will react the moment you make your move.
Have the damage control teams ready in advance.
There's no way to avoid the incoming volley entirely. The best you can do is minimize the damage. That cost is unavoidable, and you've already accounted for it.
Gray First Officer
Understood!

Three minutes later, cannon fire erupts to the north, its thunder seeming to shake the fog itself.
The flagship accelerates, and the vibration of its engines rolls through the deck. You grip the bridge railing and watch your position move steadily toward the main channel exit.

The destroyer formation bursts from the northern exit at full speed, trains its guns on the port side of Red's battleship, and unleashes three rapid volleys. Then it turns at once and disappears back into the reefs.

On Red's side...
Red First Officer
Ma'am! The battleship on our left has been hit! Its port-side weapons are offline!
Adelyde
Send in damage control immediately. Destroyers, fill the gap.
Her voice remains steady as she marks the new positions on the chart.
The two starboard interceptors are already racing toward the main channel exit—
Red First Officer
Gray's flagship has crossed the central deep-water channel at full speed! It's clear of the reefs and closing on the main channel exit!
Adelyde
How long until our starboard ships can intercept?
Red First Officer
They're closing in. Three minutes to the intercept point!
Three minutes. Gray's flagship will reach the anchorage in less than two.
They're one minute too late.
Adelyde
Starboard destroyers, don't wait to reach the intercept point. Open fire on the Gray flagship's starboard side and disrupt its anchoring maneuver.
Red First Officer
Understood!

The two sides exchange fire at the main channel exit. Cannon blasts tear through the fog, briefly outlining both ships in flashes of light.

Gray's flagship takes a hit to starboard, damaging its outer armor and forcing it to pause its first anchoring maneuver. The hull remains intact, however, and after a brief evasive maneuver, it secures the anchorage and blocks the narrowest point of the channel.
One of Red's starboard destroyers is hit in return. Taking on water along its starboard side, it is forced to withdraw and rejoin the formation.
Both sides suffer losses.

Red's left battleship has lost part of its port-side firepower, and one starboard destroyer has returned damaged. Gray's flagship has taken a hit to starboard, while one destroyer from the northern strike has run aground during its retreat and is temporarily immobilized.
At the main channel exit, Gray's flagship holds firm, fresh shell scars across its hull.
The battle enters a new round of calculations.

Adelyde
They've sealed the main channel exit. Well played.
Adelyde
They can now hold the position with less effort while preventing us from splitting our forces.
Adelyde
A direct assault on the exit would force our battleships to expose their broadsides to the enemy's guns.
Adelyde
They've left us no opening.
Adelyde
First officer.
Red First Officer
Yes!
Adelyde
All ships hold their current positions. Prioritize damage control and report combat readiness one vessel at a time.
Red First Officer
Understood!
Reports arrive one after another. Adelyde listens to each and updates the chart as she goes.
The enemy flagship is anchored but damaged. One destroyer has run aground to the north, and the rest of their forces inside the reefs can't deploy in large numbers either.

Even after Adelyde saw through the feint and set up an interception, her opponent found a window narrower than the one she'd allowed for. Three movements unfolded at once, each timed to support the next. They used the terrain about as effectively as anyone could.
A sequence like that is only possible when every move has been planned before the first order is given.
Adelyde
Even for an experienced officer, that would've been an excellent operation.

Red First Officer
Ma'am, what do we do next...?
Adelyde
We wait for the fog to clear.
The enemy now controls every advantageous position along the channel. The reef belt has become their territory, with the fog serving as a natural shield around it.
Once visibility improves and Red's firing accuracy returns, much of that advantage will disappear.
After the first officer leaves, Adelyde stands alone, looking at the binoculars beside the chart.
Adelyde
They know how to use the terrain, and they aren't afraid to commit.
In all her years as an instructor, Adelyde has seen many talented students. Very few, however, have made it this far.
They've turned what should've been a rout into a stalemate.
Reading the enemy's intentions is crucial in battle. Adelyde often studies the field from her opponent's perspective so she can prepare the best response.
This opponent's thinking is remarkably close to her own.
Adelyde
Every stalemate breaks eventually. Which of us will find the opening first?
